summary: Facepalm: Searched UPI odd news and general queries; one solid candidate found (Chicago Bean push), others set aside. Genius: The search tool turned up very little inside the Nov. 5–11 window. Phys.org was blocked, and most of the other results were older than the window or came from sources that aren't accepted. I found no genius story with a complete, accepted pair of sources, so I'm submitting none. No genius or facepalm story met the standard; nothing published.

candidates.headline: Hundreds gather in Chicago's Millennium Park to push the 110-ton Bean seven inches to the left
candidates.reason: The second source (NBC Chicago, the corroboration source) was published November 12, 2026. That is after the scan date of 2026-11-11, and source pages may not be dated after the scan date. Without it, the story has only one source (CBS News Chicago), so the two-publisher requirement is not met.; The NBC Chicago article is mainly about a Coors Light social media post that came days later. It covers the Bean push only as background, so it is weak corroboration even apart from the date.; Minor fit concern: the event was a deliberate, self-aware internet gag that participants knew would fail, so it is less a 'wait, what?' act than a staged joke. I would score it mid-range at most.

candidates.headline: Escaped piglets 'detained for fleeing and squealing' in Beaufort, S.C.
candidates.reason: Animals loose, no human act of absurdity; UPI page couldn't be opened.

candidates.headline: Rocky fans set Guinness record in Philadelphia
candidates.reason: Happened Nov. 13, after the scan date.

candidates.headline: Redding, Calif., bowler Warren Crawford rolls 243 strikes in an hour, beating the Guinness record (Nov. 11)
candidates.reason: The event is in the US and inside the window. Coverage came only from KRCR, KMPH, Action News Now and KQMS, which are local or unlisted outlets, plus Yahoo and Bowling Life. No accepted publisher turned up, and Guinness hasn't verified the record.

candidates.headline: Hundreds of 'Rocky' fans set a Guinness record for the largest gathering dressed as Rocky Balboa, Philadelphia
candidates.reason: The record was set Friday, Nov. 13, after the scan date. It is also a fan-gathering stunt.

candidates.headline: SS United States sunk off Okaloosa County, Fla., to become the world's largest artificial reef
candidates.reason: WJHG dates the sinking to Nov. 12, after the scan date. NPR's page content could not be read. It is also a reef project rather than a distinct achievement.

candidates.headline: Montana eighth-grader Rye Rost wins second place at the Thermo Fisher Junior Innovators Challenge for plantain bioplastic
candidates.reason: The competition results were announced around Oct. 27–28, before the window. The MTPR story was published Nov. 5. It is also a second-place finish.

candidates.headline: ScienceDaily items such as Yale's aging-interventions study, the SLAC/Stanford AI laser-simulation speedup, and Regensburg's quantum-jump electrons
candidates.reason: Each is a ScienceDaily repost of work published well before the window (the AI laser-simulation paper is from May, the Yale study from August), or it comes from a non-US institution (Regensburg). None has a second accepted source.
